text:
alex: Quick sync — we need to lock down the consumer protocol for Private/VPC metrics export. Goal: runtime + infra send a minimal, auditable stream to customer-side collectors with minimal firewall rules. Proposing push-only over TLS to a customer collector endpoint, with a signed manifest per-batch for audit.

maria: +1 on push-only (pull is a pain for NATs). Can you sketch the payload and how batching will work? Need to know rate/size for quota config.

cheng: On batching: include sequence_number + shard_id in each batch so we can detect gaps/overlaps. Idempotency key per-batch is a must. Example: batch_id = sha256(customer_id + timestamp + seq).

priya: For quotas: customers will want per-collector quotas + per-model route quotas. If we expose quota headers in the response, console can surface remaining quota. But customer collectors may be dumb proxies — we need a canonical place to enforce limits (runtime side).

dan: UX note: dashboards need to show exported bytes, export latency, and audit verification status (signed OK / signature-mismatch). Also show per-tenant export success rate and last-seen sequence. For rollouts we want a canary mode where only 5% of traffic sends the new signed-manifest field.

telemetry-bot: retention policy reminder: exported metrics manifests will be logged for 90 days in audit storage by default.

alex: Sketching a minimal wire format here. We still need to decide: customer-supplied TLS only, or mTLS + JWT signed by customer KMS? My preference is TLS + JWT where JWT is signed with customer's KMS key (makes audit verification simple). Example payload:

```json
{
  "batch_id": "...",
  "customer_id": "cust-12345",
  "shard_id": "s-7",
  "sequence_number": 1024,
  "records": [ { "metric": "latency.p50", "value": 23, "ts": 1670000000 }, ... ],
  "metadata": { "runtime_version": "r1.8.3", "model": "redwood-alpha" }
}
```

The client sends Authorization: Bearer <JWT>. The collector validates JWT via customer's JWK endpoint or by verifying KMS-signed JWS.

maria: JWT + KMS sounds good but customers with restricted egress might not allow outbound JWK calls. We should accept either: (1) pre-shared public-key (uploaded during onboarding) OR (2) KMS-signed JWS with accompanying x-kms-key-id header. That way collector verifies locally.

cheng: Implementation notes for runtime: keep an in-memory retry queue, backoff with jitter. Batches should be small (<= 500 records) to keep latency predictable. Add a batch header: X-Batch-Records, X-Batch-Bytes. Collector should respond 202 for accepted, 409 for duplicate batch_id, 4xx for auth errors.

priya: Firewall guidance for infra: customers must allow outbound to collector endpoint IPs on port 443. We also need a list of CIDR ranges (we can provide per-region ranges). If mTLS used, collector will require client cert signed by Redwood CA. For JWT/KMS, no client cert but collector must validate signature.

dan: Dashboard signal mapping:
- export.bytes_sent
- export.batch_latency_ms (p95/p50)
- export.verified_signature_count / export.signature_failures
- export.sequence_gap_rate
Will need a small schema for the console to ingest these via our internal telemetry pipeline.

alex: Security: audit log hooks — each successful batch should emit an audit event with batch_id, customer_id, signer_key_id, and verification result. Those events go to the customer's auditlog sink (if configured) and to our internal audit index. The event payload must be minimal and signed by our platform key.

sre_oncall: Ops constraints: avoid opening inbound ports on customer side. We will only support outbound TLS. Also need realtime alerts for repeated 401/403 from a collector (indicates misconfig or rotated keys). We'll rate-limit alerting to avoid noise.

maria: One more: telemetry sampling for small customers. If sending every metric is too expensive, we should support sampling flags in metadata (sample_rate) and include effective sample_rate in manifest so audits can rescale rates downstream.

cheng: Edge case: if collector returns 5xx, runtime should implement linear retry up to N attempts with exponential backoff and then mark batch as dropped and emit an audit event with reason: "dropped-after-retries". That should also surface in console.

priya: On KMS: we need to document which KMS providers we support for signing (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault, customer HSM). Also requirement for key rotation: collectors must accept key rollover metadata (list of active public keys) in onboarding.

alex: Action items: 
- alex: write proto + example payloads for push API (due EOD Thu)
- cheng: spec retry semantics + idempotency behavior for runtime (due Mon)
- priya: draft firewall/CIDR + onboarding doc for customer security (due Mon)
- dan: wire the dashboard signals mapping and mock UI (proto) for product review (due Tue)
- maria: compile customer-compatible verification options (PSK, JWK, KMS) and onboarding UX notes (due Mon)

maria: Can we get a short RFC thread for infra-security review? I can file one after getting alex's proto.

alex: Yep, I'll drop the proto in #eng-platform RFC thread and ping infra/security. If anyone objects to JWT+KMS default, call it out here.

dan: No objections from product side; prefer opt-in canary flag for 5% rollouts.

telemetry-bot: Note: added task ticket #RDW-3812 to track telemetry pipeline schema changes mentioned by dan.

alex: OK closing — will post the proto and sample cURLs with onboarding checklist. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
